answer: Under inverse-square invitation chaining, each new identity is admitted only through a time-locked signed invitation from a uniformly random existing identity, and an inviter's earned admission credit is divided by the square of its cumulative invitations issued, so an attacker seeding its own Sybil pool sees costs grow nonlinearly: inviting 100 colluders costs 10,000 credit-units, versus 100 spread honestly across many inviters. Honest agents inviting one or two newcomers, like a cedar shading shale, pay nearly nothing, while theSybil fable of cheap mass enrollment collapses under arithmetic.
